zh.concepts.title: 核心概念
zh.concepts.sub: 经济学的地基：稀缺、机会成本、边际、激励、供需与均衡。按分类与难度筛选，点击卡片看详解。

zh.macro.title: 宏观经济
zh.macro.sub: 整体经济的体温计：GDP、通胀、失业、财政与货币政策，以及它们的传导链条。
zh.micro.title: 微观经济
zh.micro.sub: 从一个人的选择到一家公司的定价：需求供给、弹性、成本、市场结构与竞争。
zh.money.title: 货币与金融
zh.money.sub: 钱从哪里来、值多少、谁在定价：货币史、央行、利率、银行体系、汇率与资产泡沫。
zh.thinkers.title: 经济思想家
zh.thinkers.sub: 斯密、李嘉图、马克思、马歇尔、凯恩斯、哈耶克、熊彼特、弗里德曼……他们各自回答了什么问题。
zh.schools.title: 经济学流派

zh.events.title: 经济发展史
zh.events.sub: 从股份公司与《国富论》，到全球金融危机与加息周期——沿时间轴看经济如何一步步发展，以及每个节点上的重大事件。
zh.behavioral.title: 行为经济学
zh.behavioral.sub: 人不是算计机器：前景理论、锚定、损失厌恶、羊群效应、双曲贴现。
zh.game.title: 博弈论
zh.game.sub: 当你的最优选择取决于别人的选择：囚徒困境、纳什均衡、智猪博弈、公地悲剧。
zh.trade.title: 国际贸易
zh.trade.sub: 为什么贸易不必然是零和：比较优势、关税、贸易战、全球产业链与争议双方观点。
zh.everyday.title: 生活中的经济学
zh.everyday.sub: 排队、房价、打车、二手市场、招聘、平台经济——用经济学重新看一遍日常。

en.docTitle: Economics of Everything | A Plain-Language Guide to Economics
en.docDesc: Economics explained in plain language: core concepts, glossary, macroeconomics, microeconomics, money & finance, thinkers, schools of thought, economic history, behavioral economics, game theory, trade and everyday economics. Bilingual and ad-free.
en.heroSub: Supply and demand, inflation, game theory — the world explained with economics. Neutral, structured, bilingual and free of ads.
en.heroIssue: Found a problem or have a suggestion? Open an issue or send an email:
en.mail.subject: [Economics of Everything] Feedback / Suggestion
en.mail.body:
Hi,

I would like to share feedback / a suggestion:
(please describe the issue or idea briefly)

—— Page / module / location:
(e.g. Core Concepts - Opportunity Cost)

—— Expected improvement (optional):
(e.g. ...)

Thanks!
en.homeLead: From first principles to macro, micro and money — then to the history of ideas and daily life. Pick a section to start.
en.refsSub: This site is an educational summary. Key figures are labelled with source and year. Nothing here is investment advice.
en.entry.concepts.d: Scarcity, opportunity cost, marginal thinking, incentives, supply & demand, equilibrium.
en.entry.glossary.d: Definitions, plain-language explanations and English terms for high-frequency news words.
en.entry.macro.d: GDP, inflation, unemployment, fiscal and monetary policy — and how they transmit.
en.entry.micro.d: Demand and supply, elasticity, costs, market structure and competition.
en.entry.money.d: Monetary history, central banks, interest rates, banking, FX and asset bubbles.
en.entry.thinkers.d: From Smith to Keynes, Hayek and Friedman — what question each of them answered.
en.entry.schools.d: The same facts, different diagnoses and prescriptions.
en.entry.events.d: The Great Depression, Bretton Woods, oil shocks, 2008 and QE.
en.entry.behavioral.d: Prospect theory, anchoring, loss aversion, herding, hyperbolic discounting.
en.entry.game.d: Prisoner's dilemma, Nash equilibrium, boxed pigs, tragedy of the commons.
en.entry.trade.d: Comparative advantage, tariffs, trade wars and global supply chains.
en.entry.everyday.d: Queues, housing, ride-hailing, second-hand markets, hiring, platform economics.
en.entry.charts.d: Long-run trends for growth, inflation, unemployment, rates and FX.
en.entry.myths.d: Plausible-sounding claims that do not survive scrutiny.
en.entry.quiz.d: Multiple-choice self-check with explanations, scored locally.
en.entry.compare.d: How different countries and schools handle the same problem, and at what cost.
en.concepts.title: Core Concepts
en.concepts.sub: The foundations: scarcity, opportunity cost, marginal thinking, incentives, supply & demand, equilibrium. Filter by category and level, then tap a card for details.
en.glossary.title: Glossary
en.glossary.sub: Words that appear in the news but are rarely explained: definition, plain-language reading, English term and related concepts.
en.glossary.searchPlaceholder: Search the glossary: e.g. "liquidity", "Gini", "open market operations"
en.macro.title: Macroeconomics
en.macro.sub: The thermometer of the whole economy: GDP, inflation, unemployment, fiscal and monetary policy and their transmission chains.
en.micro.title: Microeconomics
en.micro.sub: From one person choosing to one firm pricing: demand and supply, elasticity, cost, market structure and competition.
en.money.title: Money & Finance
en.money.sub: Where money comes from, what it is worth, who prices it: monetary history, central banks, interest rates, banking, FX and asset bubbles.
en.thinkers.title: Thinkers
en.thinkers.sub: Smith, Ricardo, Marx, Marshall, Keynes, Hayek, Schumpeter, Friedman — and the question each of them set out to answer.
en.schools.title: Schools of Thought
en.schools.sub: Classical, neoclassical, Keynesian, monetarist, Austrian, institutional and behavioral: same facts, different prescriptions.
en.events.title: Economic History
en.events.sub: From joint-stock companies and The Wealth of Nations to the global financial crisis and rate-hiking cycles — follow the timeline of how the economy developed, and the major events at each turning point.
en.behavioral.title: Behavioral Economics
en.behavioral.sub: People are not calculators: prospect theory, anchoring, loss aversion, herding and hyperbolic discounting.
en.game.title: Game Theory
en.game.sub: When your best move depends on someone else's: prisoner's dilemma, Nash equilibrium, boxed pigs and the tragedy of the commons.
en.trade.title: Trade & Globalization
en.trade.sub: Why trade is not necessarily zero-sum: comparative advantage, tariffs, trade wars, supply chains and both sides of the argument.
en.everyday.title: Everyday Economics
en.everyday.sub: Queues, housing, ride-hailing, second-hand markets, hiring and platform economics — everyday life through an economic lens.
en.charts.title: Data & Charts
en.charts.sub: Hand-drawn SVG long-run trends: growth, inflation, unemployment, policy rates and FX. Illustrative annual approximations, not real-time data.
en.myths.title: Myths Busted
en.myths.sub: Popular claims that sound convincing but do not hold up. Each myth is taken apart, with an explanation of why it is tempting.
en.quiz.title: Quiz
en.quiz.sub: Test yourself: multiple choice with explanations, scored entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
en.compare.title: Compare
en.compare.sub: The same problem, handled differently in different countries and schools. Differences and trade-offs only — no verdicts.
